first: A long table. Scales of every size. The Assayer does not look up. "First time? Sit. This won't take long, and it will not hurt more than it already has."
The Assayer sets your blood on the smallest scale and makes a note. "{name}. New ledger. Everyone gets one eventually."
choleric: The Assayer weighs your yellow bile and the needle runs hot. "You died angry. Most do. I'll put a little less of that back."
"Choleric to the last." The Assayer fans the pan to cool it. "You burn bright and you burn short, {name}."
"Too much yellow." The Assayer pours some off into a jar already full of it. "Everyone thinks the fire is the strong part."
melancholic: The black bile settles in the pan like ink. "So heavy," says the Assayer, not unkindly. "Were you guarding something, or just tired?"
"Melancholic." The Assayer tips the scale back towards level. "The cold kept you alive longer than you think. Not long enough, clearly."
The Assayer holds your black bile up to a light that isn't there. "Dense. I'll lend you some warmth. You'll want to give it back eventually."
balanced: The scales settle almost level. The Assayer frowns at them. "Balanced, and dead anyway. Annoying for both of us."
"Even measures." The Assayer writes something short. "Try again with the same recipe. Or don't. I only keep the books."
The Assayer weighs each humour in turn, and hands them back in the same order. "Mind the doorway. It's lower than it looks."
frequent: "{name}." The Assayer turns a page without looking. "Death number {deaths}. I've started keeping your ledger closer to hand."
The Assayer has your scales out before you arrive. "I took the liberty."
